object_description: low polygonal pavilion volume set in the park following the natural topography
geometry_property: shingled facade with sheet metal roof
design_condition: the volume sits in the park subtly following the natural topography, its polygonal shape breaking the facades to reduce the scale of the large footprint and encourage indoor-outdoor relations

positive: The structure is set in the park subtly following the natural topography of the land
The polygonal shape breaks up the facades and reduces the scale of the large footprint
The low heights reduce the impact and encourage indoor-outdoor relations
A new pedestrian walkway links station and church, articulating the various plazas
The communal areas benefit from level access directly linked to the future school
The new esplanade gives a new quality to the space linked to the church belvedere
The wall-lined path becomes rich and varied
The functions are judiciously distributed, with an external extension of the esplanade from the living areas
Alternating secondary and service rooms structure the play and distribution areas
Circulation is generous and linked to the outdoor pedestrian walkway
Natural lighting is generally of high quality
A void keeps the two care areas connected while their checkrooms stay independent
The refectory placed half a level higher provides an interesting synergy of use
Kitchen deliveries can be served independently
The architectural expression is consistent with the layout
Large surfaces are offset by well-dimensioned glazing, low excavation and the use of wood
The project takes into account and structures the site as a whole, reading as a pavilion development in the park
negative: Using stairs to bridge the level difference does not guarantee access for deliveries, services or snow clearance
The position of the external parking compromises access and outdoor space for the future school
The use of wooden shingles on the facade is questionable, especially against the sheet metal roof
The fifth facade has a significant impact seen from the station
The project falls into the category of expensive, high-volume schemes, partly due to its generous corridors and changing rooms
Questions are raised about fire standards in the compartments and about the shingled facades
The large surface area of roof, facades and floors and the significant footprint weigh on sustainability
